In order to have a proper discussion about the pricing of video game ports, you need to pose an argument with games that have similar circumstances. Using a popular platformer as your argument against the pricing of a specific port is easy to pick apart. That platformer is available on multiple platforms, each with varying market shares. It is priced at $40 because the markets for those platforms are much larger. The MSRP was set at this price likely because they determined that the game would not be able to compete as well in all those different markets had it been set at $60.

Now I know the specific port was initially $50 upon release and is now $20 as a select title, but there’s a reason why it wasn’t $60 in the first place. The game released in the first quarter of 2014 after being delayed from the fourth quarter of 2013. The game was delayed most likely due to financial reporting concerns. The first quarter of 2014 was bleak as hell. That game was literally the only title in a vast sea of nothing being offered from its publisher at the time. They needed that game to be released in the first quarter of 2014 (and not the fourth quarter of 2013 which already had other major titles propping it up) and they needed to have the game sell *in that quarter*. So the reason why it was likely $50 from the start is because they desperately needed to incentivize buyers into picking up the game sooner than later.

So with that information in mind, to answer your question, they can sell that port at $60 now because they can. Bottom line. And it’s selling like crazy. It was the number one game in Japan in the month of May and it’s outselling the previous version - no contest. This is simple economics. The game is priced in accordance with the consumers' willingness to pay, and apparently consumers are willing to pay. Price drop? Not happening. This game will probably be $60 for years to come. This game cannot be found on other major platforms and it doesn’t have to share its market share with nearly as many third parties as the popular platformer on multiple markets.
